Hi everyone! I’m Sahar Anam, LLPC, a Michigan therapist providing telehealth therapy to adults throughout Michigan in English and Arabic.

I work with adults who are navigating anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship concerns, parenting challenges, stress, and major life transitions. I’m also developing a specialty in perinatal mental health and have completed training through Postpartum Support International.

As an Arabic speaking therapist, I’m especially passionate about making therapy more accessible to Arabic speaking individuals and families who may have difficulty finding a therapist they feel comfortable communicating with.

My clinical experience also includes working with women affected by domestic violence during my internship at Access Community Health in Dearborn, which deepened my passion for providing compassionate, empowering, and trauma informed care.

I’m currently welcoming new adult clients through telehealth and would be happy to connect with other providers who are looking for a therapist to refer to. 🤍

Psychology Today:
[https://www.psychologytoday.com/profile/1782199](https://www.psychologytoday.com/profile/1782199)

Looking forward to connecting with everyone and being part of this community! 🌿

**(Texas & California) Clinical Consultation Group: Starting in Oct.**

***Looking for more depth, connection, and fresh perspective in your clinical work?***

Some of the most important growth as a therapist happens in conversation with other clinicians—when there’s space to bring the cases that stay with you, think beyond a single model or technique, and consider possibilities you may not have seen on your own.

I’m starting a new Clinical Development Consultation Group this October for emerging- to mid-career, independently licensed therapists who want to deepen their clinical thinking while building meaningful connections with other clinicians.

I bring more than two decades of experience facilitating clinical consultation and supporting therapists’ professional development, including many years as a Clinical Director overseeing and developing a large clinical team.

This biweekly group offers a warm, collaborative, and engaging space to explore complex cases, therapeutic challenges and impasses, case conceptualization, clinical strategies and interventions, theory and technique, and the therapeutic relationship. We’ll draw from a variety of clinical models and perspectives, with an emphasis on developing greater depth, confidence, and intentionality in your work.

The group is $65 per meeting, and CEUs are provided for Texas clinicians. The group meets biweekly, Tuesdays, 11:45-1 pm CST/9:45 am-11 am PST.

Interested in learning more or seeing if the group might be a good fit? Reach out to me at [Therapy@SeannaCrosbie.com](mailto:Therapy@SeannaCrosbie.com).

***“When I came across Seanna's group, I had been searching and searching for a consultation group that offered what I was needing…an expectation of affirming and justice-based care, a closed group, and one that was consistently safe and supportive. What I've found has been this and so much more! No longer do I feel like an island on my own in private practice, but instead, like a professional with a support group who gets it and wants to help.” – Clinician  ***

🚪 **THE GATE, NOT THE WALL**

**Mastering Self-Advocacy in Supervision**

How do counselors advocate for their professional and clinical capacity **without apologizing for appropriate boundaries?**

Join us for October’s **Lunch & Learn Webinar** to explore the **“Sandwich Method,”** a practical framework for ethical self-advocacy in supervision and the workplace. Through live scripting and modeling, participants will practice moving from **apology-based communication to capacity-based boundary setting**—helping protect clinical energy, client safety, and career longevity.

📅 **Thursday, October 15, 2026**
⏰ **11:00 AM–12:00 PM ET**
💻 **Live via Zoom**
🎓 **1 NBCC Credit Hour**

**Presenters:**
Dr. Kellie Forziat-Pytel, Ph.D., LPC-PA, NCC, ACS
Ashley Graff, BS, CMHC Graduate Student

**Participants will learn to:**

✔ Use the **Sandwich Method** to validate, establish a firm clinical boundary, and offer a professional pivot.
✔ Replace apology-based language with **capacity-based communication** during high-stakes situations.
✔ Maintain appropriate boundaries when faced with systemic pushback or secondary requests.

**💲 Accessible & Affordable CE**

**CCU Students, Faculty/Staff & Current Counseling Site Supervisors:** FREE
**CCU Alumni:** $4/session | $31 full series
**Mental Health Providers & Others:** $5/session | $40 full series

💙 **Giving Back:** Proceeds support CCU students in need of off-campus mental health and wellness services.

A simple move for the next time you go blank in session.

 

Before you search for the right thing to say, pause three seconds.

Then ask yourself one question:

What is this moment actually asking of me?

Not what should I do. Not what would a better therapist say. Just, what does this moment need?

That question can create just enough space between reacting and responding.

It's also the foundation of the work I teach inside the Clinical Skills & Confidence Field Guides.

 

Guide 1 — What To Do When You Don't Know What To Say in Session — $27

 

A practical tool for the moments that don't come with a script.

 

https://wayseekercoaching.com/guideno1

Hi all!! Call for Appalachian Counselors!!
My name is Preston Mannon, and I am a doctoral learner in Capella University’s Counselor Education and Supervision program.

The purpose of this research is to better understand counselors’ experiences, challenges, and perspectives when working with LGBTQ+ clients in the Appalachian region.

You may be eligible to participate if you:

·       Are a licensed counselor (e.g., Licensed Professional Counselor, Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor, Licensed Mental Health Counselor, or equivalent state-recognized counseling license).

·       Have experience providing counseling services to LGBTQ+ clients within the Appalachian region.

You are not eligible to participate if you:

·       Are currently under investigation for ethical or licensure violations.

·       Hold a counseling license that is inactive, suspended, restricted, or otherwise not in good standing at the time of recruitment.

 

What Participation Involves-

Completion of a brief Google Form screening

A 10–15 minute email or phone screening (if eligible)

One 45-60 minute virtual interview conducted via Zoom

Audio recording of the interview for research purposes

 

Time Commitment

Total participation time is approximately 60–75 minutes.

 

How to Participate

To express interest, please complete the screening form:

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScTeCZ-e4IRVGG03MzAvbXY-HJr-gKvIemhTgDkyudeb5RgWQ/viewform

 

Please note: Participation is voluntary. You may decline to participate or withdraw at any time without penalty.

You are welcome to share this invitation with other counselors who may meet the eligibility criteria.

Contact Information

If you have questions or would like additional information, please contact:

Email: PMannon@capellauniversity.edu
